title: Voice: tap during SPEAKING leaves userActivated armed (zombie state)
description: VoiceViewModel.toggle() routes SPEAKING -> interrupt() which flushes audio and sets state=LISTENING, but does NOT clear userActivated. Every other deactivate path (LISTENING-tap, CONNECTING-tap, disconnect) clears it. Result: user taps mic mid-Gemini-response to deactivate, visually sees the icon transition past (purple SPEAKING -> green-pulse LISTENING), assumes voice is off; meanwhile mic is still armed (userActivated=true). Next status change (e.g., bumping incline) pushes context to Gemini via updateStateContext, Gemini emits an audio response, onAudioChunk's gate 'if (!userActivated) return' lets it through, audio plays unexpectedly. Two related zombie paths: line 362 (mic permission denied -> IDLE) and line 379 (teardownConnection -> IDLE) also leave userActivated=true. Fix (Option A from investigation): SPEAKING-tap is treated as deactivate everywhere else; mirror that. interrupt() becomes dead code (will be removed in a follow-up). Verify on tablet: tap mic, talk, while Gemini speaks tap again, confirm mic icon goes inactive (no green pulse), bump incline, no audio fires.
acceptance_criteria: In SPEAKING state, mic tap clears userActivated and goes to IDLE; mic icon shows inactive; bumping incline triggers no audible Gemini response. Same for line 362 + 379 paths.
close_reason: Two-part bug, both fixed: (1) tap during SPEAKING left userActivated armed (interrupt() path didn't deactivate); (2) server-side 'interrupted' signal arriving in response to silent context pushes (incline bumps) bounced voiceState back to LISTENING via the ungated onInterrupted callback, lighting the mic icon as 'active' even though audio was correctly dropped. Fix: SPEAKING toggle branch mirrors LISTENING (clear userActivated, flush, IDLE); onInterrupted now gated on userActivated; line 362 (mic perm fail) and line 379 (teardownConnection) also clear userActivated as belt-and-suspenders cleanup. Verified live on tablet (SM-X115): 5 post-deactivation server INTERRUPTED signals captured, each shows onInterrupted with voiceState=IDLE, state held.

title: Self-signed HTTPS for commissioned Pis + client trust
description:
Commissioned DietPi Pis are HTTP-only: provisioning never installs Tailscale, and setup.sh's only cert path is 'tailscale cert'. iOS (Treddy) cannot connect at all (ATS blocks cleartext); Android only worked via usesCleartextTraffic. Decision: drop Tailscale, generate a per-device self-signed cert on the Pi at setup time (clients already trust-all). 

DONE (hot-fix, verified end-to-end on live rpi-zero): on-device openssl self-signed cert, treadmill-server HTTPS; Android AppModule.kt trustAllTls() X509TrustManager (was hostnameVerifier-only -> CertPathValidatorException).

REMAINING: (1) setup.sh: replace Tailscale block with idempotent on-device self-signed generation + add openssl prereq; (2) ship-check.sh: assert HTTPS not plain HTTP; (3) Kotlin JVM test infra (mockwebserver+okhttp-tls) + regression test for trustAllTls() against a self-signed MockWebServer (hotfixed ahead of test-first, must backfill); (4) iOS end-to-end verification on device (mechanism confirmed correct, not yet run); (5) update docs/CLAUDE.md.
notes: Core HTTPS fix SHIPPED + verified (commits 3e21412 Android trust, 3b364b7 setup.sh self-signed; live rpi-zero hot-fixed). Umbrella now tracks follow-ups via deps: precor-9_3x-3y0 (test backfill), precor-9_3x-711 (docs), precor-9_3x-ebq (mdns spec) actionable; precor-9_3x-2ef (iOS e2e) + precor-9_3x-2le (fresh-flash) deferred.

title: Distinguish program templates from run instances for user history
description: Currently a program and a run of that program are conflated. We need to separate: (1) Program template — the reusable definition (intervals, name, source), and (2) Program instance/run — a specific execution with start time, actual duration, distance, calories, etc. This enables proper user history: 'I ran Hill Climber 3 times this week' rather than just seeing the program definition in history. Saved workouts become program templates; history entries become run instances that reference a template.

title: Add 'My Workouts' section for saved user workouts

title: Engine samples full bitmap but screen uses ContentScale.Crop — sampled rects don't match rendered pixels
description: On-device verification (emulator, bright bg_forest) showed the hero timer scrim works and is legible, but the metrics row secondary text reads faint over a bright crop. Root cause: rememberRunReadability() samples the FULL decoded bg_forest bitmap at normalized rects, while RunningScreen draws it with ContentScale.Crop (fillMaxSize). On a phone aspect ratio the crop discards top/bottom (or sides), so the pixels actually behind each text block differ from what the engine sampled — the APCA guarantee becomes approximate. Fix: sample the SAME crop the UI renders (compute the crop rect for the device aspect ratio and map block rects into it), or sample after layout from the displayed region. Found during feat/adaptive-text-readability emulator QA.
close_reason: Fixed: cropMapRect maps block rects through ContentScale.Crop before sampling; pure + unit-tested; verified on emulator (portrait+landscape).

title: Wire BackgroundAdviceClient to runtime so the Gemini prior reaches the device
description: rememberRunReadability() in RunningScreen.kt currently calls chooseTheme(regions, AdvicePrior()) with a hardcoded neutral prior — the server endpoint /api/background/advise and the Kotlin BackgroundAdviceClient both exist and are tested, but are not connected. Fetch the prior off the main thread (keyed by sha256 of the background image, which is also the server cache key) and recompute the Theme when it returns, behind a remember keyed on the prior so neutral renders first then refines. APCA already guarantees legibility without it; this only adds photo-matched hue/polarity. From feat/adaptive-text-readability.

title: Apply per-region scrims to individual metric tiles (not one shared metricsScrim)
description: rememberRunReadability() computes per-region scrim alphas for speed/incline/distance/hint but only scrims['speed'] is used to drive the shared LocalGlassParams.panelOpacity, so every metric tile gets the same scrim. The engine's per-region precision is mostly unused for the metric row. Consider providing per-tile scrim (e.g. a CompositionLocal map or passing scrim into each tile) so each tile clears its own local APCA target. Low priority — tiles sit in one row over similar background, so the shared scrim is usually adequate. From feat/adaptive-text-readability.

Safe today (returns AdvicePrior() defaults, never crashes) but less granular. Make each field parse independently. Minor, from final review on feat/adaptive-text-readability.

title: Android: AnimatedContent may flash empty text during encouragement exit animation
description:
In RunningScreen.kt, AnimatedContent now keys on encouragement != null (Boolean) to avoid bounce animation on every countdown tick. However, inside the showEncouragement == true branch, the code reads encouragement directly from compose state rather than from the animated target state.

During the exit animation (encouragement to timer transition), encouragement may already be null while the exit animation is still rendering. glowText(encouragement ?: "") would briefly show empty text before the fade completes.

Impact: Unlikely to be visible given the fast spring animation (dampingRatio=0.6f), but could cause a brief blank flash if the device is under load.

Affected code: RunningScreen.kt lines ~157 and ~424 (portrait and landscape).

Potential fix: Cache the last non-null encouragement value in a remember block and use that inside the AnimatedContent lambda, so the exit animation always has text to display.
